newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Hang Seng jumps to record close.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Hang Seng jumps to record close.

text.p: A surge in property stocks led Hong Kong's Hang Seng index to a record close on Wednesday, with investors encouraged by the outlook for both interest rates and the property market, analysts said.
The Hang Seng index closed up 137.38 points at 12,943.69, after hitting a record intra-day peak at 12,951.85. Turnover was HK$7.83 billion compared with Tuesday's HK$6.88 billion.

"People are reasonably bullish on property and by extension to a certain extent banking," said Alan Hutcheson, director of research at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. "There is a Fed meeting tonight and people are assuming the result before the event."

The U.S. Federal Reserve is due to meet later on Wednesday and analysts said investors were expecting interest rates to remain steady. They said the U.S. long bond yield, which fell to an eight-month low on Tuesday, was pointing in the right direction. The long bond rose 27/32 to yield 6.44 percent.
"People have looked at the U.S. market, looked at the bond market," said James Osborn, sales director at ING Barings.
"Basically there is no reason to sell it and Hong Kong, valuation wise, is certainly not overstretched," he said.
Osborn said investors may start "questioning the fundamentals" once the index hits 13,400 to 13,600 points.
"There is still some international buying but more importantly there are no real sellers," he added.

Shares in Cheung Kong rose HK$1.00 to HK$66.25 and Sun Hung Kai Properties advanced HK$1.25 to HK$89.75. Henderson Land gained HK$0.75 to HK$71.25. "There has been some uptick in prices and there has also been a lot more big volume transactions in the property sector," said Hutcheson.
Sino Land bought a 4,206-square-metre site in Yuen Long in the New Territories for HK$370 at a government land auction on Wednesday. Analysts had forecast a price of HK$260 million to HK$320 million.
"It's a pretty full price for it," said Martin Tacon, analyst at CS First Boston.
China toll road operator Anhui Expressway made its market debut on Wednesday and closed below the HK$1.77 per share initial public offering price at HK$1.58.
HSBC Holdings rose HK$1.50 to HK$162.00 and Hang Seng Bank advanced HK$1.25 to HK$96.25. Hutchison rose HK$1.25 to HK$58.75.
November Hang Seng futures ended the session 167 points higher at 12,935.
